description.narrative: Detta bidrag avser den sista fasen i utvecklingssamarbetet som har genomförts gemensamt av det serbiska inrikesministeriet (MoI) och Svenska Polismyndigheten (SPA) med Sida-finansiering sedan 2003. Det övergripande målet för programmet är att förbättra den serbiska polisens förmåga att möta internationella bästa praxis och mänskliga rättigheter.

The contribution concerns the last and final phase in development cooperation that has been jointly implemented by the Serbian Ministry of Interior (MoI) and the Swedish Police Authority (SPA) with Sida funding since 2003. The overall objective of the program is the enhanced capacity of the Serbian Police to meet international best practices and human rights standards.

The overall objective of the program is the enhanced capacity of the Serbian Police to meet international best practices and human rights standards.
There are three specific objectives related to the three thematic components. They are as follows:
Specific objective 1: Improved forensic capacities in scene of crime investigations in line with international standards, to enhance professionalism and transparency;
Specific objective 2: Ensure sustainability and improved quality of intelligence-led policing in order to improve the responsiveness and transparency and
Specific objective 3: Contribute to establishing a National Criminal Intelligence System to increase effectiveness and professionalism.

title.narrative: Grant Arrangement between The Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, Sida and The Swedish Police Authority regarding Swedish Support to Police Reform in Serbia 2025-2027
Beslut om Insats POLIS REFORM PROGRAM FAS 5, 2025-­2027

description.narrative:
The program demonstrates strong implementation performance in its first year, with a high delivery rate and effective cooperation between partners. Results are primarily at output and early outcome level, with clear capacity gains but limited evidence of systemic impact at this stage.
Progress is most advanced in the ILP component, where new tools and processes are operational in pilot sites and early behavioural change is visible. The CSI component shows solid progress in building sustainable training systems, though results have not yet translated into improved operational practice. The NCIS component remains a significant gap, with no outputs delivered due to external factors.
The contribution remains highly relevant and well aligned with reform priorities, and benefits from strong ownership and motivation within the MoI. Conditions for sustainability are being developed, particularly through training systems, but risks related to staff turnover and institutional memory persist.
Overall, the program is on track, with favourable conditions for achieving its objectives, provided that results are scaled up and institutionalized, and that gaps in the NCIS component are addressed.
Examples of concrete results
Forensics/Crime Scene Investigation (CSI)
The program has contributed to strengthening forensic capacity within the Serbian Police:
- Forensic practitioners have improved their ability to apply modern fingerprint comparison methods, with approximately half of relevant staff trained in the new non-numerical methodology,
- Institutional capacity has been strengthened through training-of-trainers approach, with around 80 trainers/mentors prepared to cascade knowledge within the organization,
- The MoI has initiated internal systems for knowledge management and sustainability, including development of e-learning materials.
While these results are primarily at capacity level, they provide a solid basis for improved investigative quality in the coming years.
Intelligence-led policing (ILP)
Progress has been made towards embedding ILP practices:
- Police units in four pilot stations have introduced daily situational analysis ("Daily Review of Public Safety"), strengthening structured decision-making and operational planning. Approximately 300 daily reviews were produced during 2025, indicating active use of new processes,
- Analytical and strategic capacity has been strengthened through the development and adoption of a Strategic Assessment on Public Safety (20262029),
- Improved information-sharing and communication has been enabled through provision of IT equipment and development of mobile solutions.
These results indicate early behavioural changes and demonstrate that ILP is being operationalized at pilot level.
National Criminal Intelligence System (NCIS)
The majority of planned activities under this component were cancelled and transferred to another donor (EU).
Program management and cross-cutting results
- Program management systems are in place, including a Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning plan and draft Communication Plan. Embassy has sent comments to the draft Communication Plan and the final draft is pending.
- Cooperation between SPA and MoI is functioning well, characterized by strong ownership, trust, and engagement.
- Progress has been made in strengthening gender equality and representation, including training of women police officers.
- SPA has developed an Exit Strategy to present the phasing out plan and related sustainability considerations.
As expected for an initial implementation year, results are primarily at output and intermediate outcome level, with gradual movement towards institutionalization.
